import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_56/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_56/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_56/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_56/training_3.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Source 0: whites_population
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Source 1: asian_population
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # Source 2: other_population
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # Source 3: mixed_population

# All source tables share these common columns: ['CountyID', 'CountyName', 'Year', 'ID']
# We will join them on these keys to form the target table.

# Rename columns in each dataframe to avoid collisions after join, according to target schema:
# Target schema columns and their source:
# - CountyID_x, CountyName_x, whites_population, Year_x, ID          <- from df0
# - CountyID_y, CountyName_y, other_population, Year_y               <- from df2
# - CountyID_x_9, CountyName_x_10, mixed_population, Year_x_12       <- from df3
# - CountyID_y_13, CountyName_y_14, asian_population, Year_y_16      <- from df1

# Rename df0 columns
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={
    'CountyID': 'CountyID_x',
    'CountyName': 'CountyName_x',
    'whites_population': 'whites_population',
    'Year': 'Year_x',
    'ID': 'ID'
})

# Rename df2 columns
df2_renamed = df2.rename(columns={
    'CountyID': 'CountyID_y',
    'CountyName': 'CountyName_y',
    'other_population': 'other_population',
    'Year': 'Year_y',
    'ID': 'ID_y'  # ID column not used in target from df2, rename to avoid collision
})

# Rename df3 columns
df3_renamed = df3.rename(columns={
    'CountyID': 'CountyID_x_9',
    'CountyName': 'CountyName_x_10',
    'mixed_population': 'mixed_population',
    'Year': 'Year_x_12',
    'ID': 'ID_x_12'  # ID column not used in target from df3, rename to avoid collision
})

# Rename df1 columns
df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={
    'CountyID': 'CountyID_y_13',
    'CountyName': 'CountyName_y_14',
    'asian_population': 'asian_population',
    'Year': 'Year_y_16',
    'ID': 'ID_y_16'  # ID column not used in target from df1, rename to avoid collision
})

# Join strategy:
# Start from df0_renamed as base (has ID column needed in target)
# Join df2_renamed on CountyID and Year (df0: CountyID_x, Year_x; df2: CountyID_y, Year_y)
# Join df3_renamed on CountyID and Year (df0: CountyID_x, Year_x; df3: CountyID_x_9, Year_x_12)
# Join df1_renamed on CountyID and Year (df0: CountyID_x, Year_x; df1: CountyID_y_13, Year_y_16)

# We join on CountyID and Year columns, matching the corresponding renamed columns.

# Merge df0 and df2
df_0_2 = pd.merge(
    df0_renamed,
    df2_renamed,
    left_on=['CountyID_x', 'Year_x'],
    right_on=['CountyID_y', 'Year_y'],
    how='inner',
    suffixes=('', '_df2')
)

# Merge the above with df3
df_0_2_3 = pd.merge(
    df_0_2,
    df3_renamed,
    left_on=['CountyID_x', 'Year_x'],
    right_on=['CountyID_x_9', 'Year_x_12'],
    how='inner',
    suffixes=('', '_df3')
)

# Merge the above with df1
df_final = pd.merge(
    df_0_2_3,
    df1_renamed,
    left_on=['CountyID_x', 'Year_x'],
    right_on=['CountyID_y_13', 'Year_y_16'],
    how='inner',
    suffixes=('', '_df1')
)

# Select and reorder columns exactly as target schema:
target_columns = [
    'CountyID_x', 'CountyName_x', 'whites_population', 'Year_x', 'ID',
    'CountyID_y', 'CountyName_y', 'other_population', 'Year_y',
    'CountyID_x_9', 'CountyName_x_10', 'mixed_population', 'Year_x_12',
    'CountyID_y_13', 'CountyName_y_14', 'asian_population', 'Year_y_16'
]

df_target = df_final[target_columns]

# Ensure correct data types as per target schema:
df_target = df_target.astype({
    'CountyID_x': 'int64',
    'CountyName_x': 'string',
    'whites_population': 'int64',
    'Year_x': 'int64',
    'ID': 'int64',
    'CountyID_y': 'int64',
    'CountyName_y': 'string',
    'other_population': 'int64',
    'Year_y': 'int64',
    'CountyID_x_9': 'int64',
    'CountyName_x_10': 'string',
    'mixed_population': 'int64',
    'Year_x_12': 'int64',
    'CountyID_y_13': 'int64',
    'CountyName_y_14': 'string',
    'asian_population': 'int64',
    'Year_y_16': 'int64'
})

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_56/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
